subject: Starter credits for FOSS Sprint Collective hackathon — request / confirmation
messages:
From: Anika Bose <anika@fossprint.org>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Request: starter credits for FOSS Sprint Collective hackathon

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well — I run community partnerships at FOSS Sprint Collective and we’re organizing a two-week virtual hackathon (Feb 14–28) focused on graph and LLM tooling. We’d love Redwood to support the event by providing small starter credits to help open-source maintainers and novice teams try hosted inference during the hack.

High-level ask: 10 promo credits for maintainers (~$300 value each) + 25 smaller trial vouchers (~$50 each) for attendees. We’ll list Redwood as a sponsor in the event page and host a short demo slot (15 minutes) during opening night.

Attached is the event proposal and expected attendee profile. Let me know what information you need to make a decision (attendee list, use-case examples, compliance questions). Ideally we’d confirm by Jan 18 so we can publish the sponsor roster.

Attachments: event-proposal.pdf (proposal, expected attendance breakdown)

Thanks — excited to partner,
Anika Bose
Community Partnerships
FOSS Sprint Collective
---
GraphBuild Org <events@graphbuild.dev>
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Request: starter credits for FOSS Sprint Collective hackathon

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding a sponsorship request from FOSS Sprint Collective. They’re asking for 10 maintainer-level credits (~$300 value each) plus 25 small trial vouchers. The event looks community-first and the organizers have partnered with GraphBuild for mentoring.

Questions:
- Do we have room in the promotions budget for 10 x $300 + 25 x $50?
- If yes, who issues the promo codes and what T&Cs should we apply (trial length, team size, abuse prevention)?
- Any compliance/red flags to raise?

I can share the attendee breakdown + use-case shortlists if helpful. They’re hoping for confirmation by Jan 18 to include Redwood in promotional materials.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Developer Relations (Community Programs)
Redwood Inference

Irene / Marissa — quick take from promos side: 10 x $300 and 25 x $50 is within the community sponsorship envelope for Q1, but I need a couple of confirmations before issuing codes:

1) Confirmed attendee/maintainer list for the 10 maintainer grants (need GitHub handles or emails).
2) Promo T&Cs: limit to one code per organization, 90-day expiration, non-transferrable — ok?
3) Do we want to route redemptions through a lightweight eligibility check (repo contribution or maintainer verification) or trust organizer sign-off?

If we do standard T&Cs and organizer attestation, I can generate the codes and share a CSV. Otherwise we should escalate to legal for a MOU.

Marking as a green light from budget perspective pending the attendee list.

—Karthik

Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: starter credits for FOSS Sprint Collective hackathon

Thanks for the ping — happy to approve the request.

Decision: Approve 10 maintainer grants at $300 each + 25 attendee vouchers at $50 each.
Conditions:
- Promo codes expire 90 days from issuance.
- One code per org/maintainer email (organizer to provide list).
- Attestation required: organizer must confirm maintainers are active project maintainers (GitHub link or similar).
- Redwood reserves right to revoke codes if we detect misuse.

Karthik — please issue codes and share promo-codes.csv with Irene and the organizer once ready. Irene — please collect the 10 maintainer emails/handles and the 25 attendee emails.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Community Programs
Redwood Inference

Looking forward to the demo slot — would love to coordinate a 15-minute opening night demo; I can present a quick walkthrough of hosted inference and best practices for low-cost development.
